input: Write a haiku a day for one month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the haikus follow a loose or strict structure (5-7-5 syllables, seasonal reference, kigo, etc.) determines how challenging each daily prompt will be and how the plan is scaffolded.
Whether the haikus are purely private, shared with a specific person, or published publicly changes the tone, polish required, and accountability structure.
Knowing which month this starts (and whether it has already begun) sets the exact timeline and total count, and seasonal themes may naturally align with real-world surroundings.
Whether there is a unifying theme (nature, emotions, daily life, a specific project) versus free-form topics each day shapes whether prompts or a content calendar are needed.
Understanding how much time per day the user can dedicate reveals whether they need a quick-draft system or have room for deeper revision and reflection.
The tool or format used to write and store haikus (notebook, app, blog, social media) determines what the daily workflow and long-term record look like.

Knowing what done-well looks like — completing all 30/31 haikus, producing a polished collection, building a habit, or sharing publicly — determines how progress is measured and what finishing the month means.

gold.taskTitle: Write a haiku every day for one month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to write one haiku per day for a full month, building a consistent daily creative writing habit.

questions.title: How strictly should each haiku follow traditional rules?
questions.description: Should every haiku follow the 5-7-5 syllable structure and include traditional elements like a seasonal reference (kigo), or is a looser, modern interpretation acceptable?

questions.title: Who will read the haikus you write?
questions.description: Are these haikus purely for yourself, meant to be shared with a specific person or group, or intended for a public audience such as a blog or social media?

questions.title: Which month are you starting, and when exactly?
questions.description: Knowing the specific month and start date sets the exact count of haikus needed and allows seasonal or calendar themes to be woven in naturally.

questions.title: Should all haikus follow one unifying theme?
questions.description: Do you want a single overarching theme — such as nature, city life, emotions, or a personal journey — or would you prefer a different topic each day with no connecting thread?

questions.title: How many minutes per day can you spend on this?
questions.description: Understanding your available daily time determines whether the plan needs a rapid-draft approach for busy days or can include time for reflection and light revision.

questions.title: Where will you write and store each haiku?
questions.description: Will you use a physical notebook, a notes app, a document, a blog, or a social media platform? This shapes the daily workflow and how the finished collection is kept.

questions.title: What does successfully completing this month look like to you?
questions.description: Is success simply writing all 30 or 31 haikus without missing a day, producing a polished shareable collection, building a lasting writing habit, or something else entirely?
